clue.text: Fishmonger's special offer for Scrooge

definitions.meaning: a fishmonger might advertise a ray-like flatfish at a bargain price: an inexpensive flatfish
Dickens's Ebenezer Scrooge, a byword for a miser

explanation.surface: A fishmonger's bargain deal laid on for the miserly Scrooge.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words, CHEAP and SKATE, and a fishmonger's bargain appears; as one word it is a stingy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser who hates spending money, like Dickens's Scrooge, is called by this slang term.

clue.text: Metal business, Latvian perhaps

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
a Balt is a native of a Baltic state, of which a Latvian is one example

explanation.surface: A metals firm, maybe based in Latvia.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a hard bluish metallic element, atomic number 27.

clue.text: Navigator's instrument with top knocked off still surviving

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed from the instrument's name

parts.note: a sextant measures angles of the sun or stars for navigation

explanation.surface: An old navigator's instrument, damaged at the top, has nonetheless survived.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extant still exists, having survived from the past.

clue.text: Influence a sprinter to cheat

parts.note: pull is influence, as in having pull with someone
a sprinter is a quick runner, a fast one

explanation.surface: Someone bribes or leans on a sprinter to cheat in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to trick or deceive someone, to get one over on them dishonestly.

clue.text: A little peck is suggested

indicators.note: only a little of the words peck is suggested is taken, a short run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A light peck hints at something more affectionate.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'peck is suggested'; the whole clue also describes the answer, a little peck.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick peck on the cheek is a small token of affection with the lips.

clue.text: Hard worker mostly tests grooming products

indicators.note: mostly means the hard worker's word loses its final letter

parts.note: a toiler is someone who labours hard
tries means tests, as in trying something out

explanation.surface: A diligent worker spends most of the time testing cosmetics.
explanation.definitionFit: Toiletries are soaps, shampoos and similar items used for washing and personal care.

clue.text: A barrier for architect

parts.note: a dam is a barrier holding back water

explanation.surface: An architect is asked to design a barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Adam was an 18th-century Scottish neoclassical architect.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Adam is a famous Scottish architect, so his surname is an example of the class.

clue.text: Neat worker repaired mainyard

indicators.note: repaired suggests the made-up word mainyard has been put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A tidy worker has fixed the main yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' looks like tidy, but here it is an old word for cattle, so a neat worker tends cows.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic word for cattle; a man who milks cows and works with dairy herds fits.

clue.text: Examination's just the thing to probe my virtue

indicators.note: to probe means to push into, so these pieces go inside the word my

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
it means exactly the thing wanted, as in 'that's it'

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a probing examination is just what their virtue needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Morality is moral goodness or principled conduct, which is what virtue is.

clue.text: Character in The Odyssey returning after the blast destroyed fighting vessel

indicators.note: after places the turned Greek letter behind the rearranged letters
destroyed suggests the words the blast are smashed and rebuilt in a new order
returning means the Greek letter is read backwards

parts.note: Homer's Odyssey is written in Greek, so a character in it is a Greek letter, here pi

explanation.surface: A figure from Homer's epic comes home after an explosion wrecked a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' is not a person in the story but a letter of the Greek alphabet the Odyssey is written in. 'destroyed' turns THE BLAST into BATTLESH; 'returning' gives IP.
explanation.definitionFit: A battleship is a large, heavily armoured warship carrying big guns.

clue.text: It takes a stiff pint by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word for a pint is said aloud, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer

explanation.surface: A stiff drink, a pint, is what someone needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' looks like a strong drink, but here it is slang for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A bier is a stand on which a coffin or corpse is placed, so it carries a dead body.

clue.text: Believe sailor's justification for advance

parts.note: to credit a story is to believe it
a rating is an ordinary sailor in the navy, not an officer

explanation.surface: Trust the sailor's reasons for moving forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' is a loan, not a forward move.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender checks a borrower's score of financial reliability before deciding to lend money.

clue.text: Arrive by gold carriage

parts.note: to land is to arrive, as a plane does
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Someone turns up in a gilded carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: Payment from trade about to unravel somewhat

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the trade word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a deal is a trade or bargain
to fray is to begin to come apart, to unravel a little at the edges

explanation.surface: A payment from business dealings begins to fall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' looks like it hints at a hidden word, but it belongs to the fraying.
explanation.definitionFit: Defrayal is the act of paying costs or expenses, so it is a payment.

clue.text: Quickly dismiss parody on solicitor protecting the French

indicators.note: on places the parody above the next piece in this down entry

parts.note: a skit is a short comic parody

indicators.note: protecting means one word wraps around the other to shield it

parts.note: a tout solicits custom, for instance for tickets
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A satirical sketch about a lawyer guarding the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' looks like a lawyer, but here it is someone who solicits custom. The answer is cricket slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, bowling out a batting side rapidly for few runs, like knocking down pins, is this phrase.

clue.text: Certain bet's stupid without right means to pay

parts.note: a banker is a racing or pools bet thought certain to win

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the stupid word goes round the other piece

parts.note: daft means stupid

explanation.surface: A sure bet is foolish if there is no proper way to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank-guaranteed cheque is a secure method of payment for large sums.

clue.text: Master arranged education sorted by ability

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the word master are set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster arranged lessons with pupils grouped by ability.
explanation.definitionFit: British schools that stream pupils place them in classes according to their ability.

clue.text: Extremely studious person bags top-class award

parts.note: best as an adverb means to the greatest degree, most of all

indicators.note: bags means captures, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: the owl stands for a wise, bookish person
A is the top grade or class

explanation.surface: A very hard-working student scoops a first-rate prize.
explanation.definitionFit: A bestowal is the act of conferring something such as an honour, or the gift so given.

clue.text: Form of cricket in which score is doubled

indicators.note: is doubled means the number word is written out twice

parts.note: a score is twenty

explanation.surface: A cricket format where the runs scored are double.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like runs, but it is the old word for the number twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the short game in which each team bats for a limited twenty overs.

clue.text: Border with Italy shelters popular Adriatic resort

indicators.note: shelters means gives cover to, so these pieces wrap around another

parts.note: a rim is a border or edge

in means popular or fashionable

explanation.definitionFit: Rimini is a seaside town on Italy's Adriatic coast, famous for its beaches.

clue.text: Group in church make obeisance

indicators.note: in places the group inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
a ring is a group or gang

explanation.surface: A congregation in church bows in reverence.
explanation.definitionFit: To grovel or bow down servilely is to show exaggerated deference.

clue.text: Snare fish after net is broken

indicators.note: after places the fishing word behind the rearranged letters
is broken suggests the word net is torn up and rearranged

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: An angler tries to fish after the net has torn.
explanation.definitionFit: To entangle is to catch or trap something, as in a web or net.

clue.text: Artillerymen landing weapon

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery
a pier is a landing stage for boats

explanation.surface: Gunners come ashore carrying their arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapier is a slender, sharp-pointed sword used for thrusting.

clue.text: Penny, out of sorts, needs this

definitions.text: Penny, out of sorts, needs this

parts.note: ill means unwell or out of sorts

explanation.surface: Penny is feeling unwell and needs some medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: what a poorly Penny needs.

clue.text: Millions have got cut

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
to own something is to have got it

explanation.surface: Millions of people have had something cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass that has been mowed has been cut down short.

clue.text: Working in Capitol I could be Congressman

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of in Capitol I being set in motion and reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone working in the Capitol could be a member of Congress.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Congress is an elected lawmaker, a professional in public office.

clue.text: Discharge lieutenant for dope

parts.note: to discharge a duty is to do it, to perform it

explanation.surface: A lieutenant is discharged from the army for being a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like drugs, but here it means a stupid person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dope is a stupid person, a fool or idiot.

clue.text: Pillar of the underground in prison having served time

indicators.note: served suggests time dished out in a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A pillar of the criminal underworld who has done time in prison.

explanation.definitionFit: A stalagmite is a column of mineral deposit rising from a cave floor.
